name: aether
description: Aether mode for Claude Code, built for RADAR: rapid, autonomous, delegating, affordable and robust. The Lead starts on Sonnet and is the owner's right hand: it understands the intent, writes the owner's intent card, and launches /aether:design, which runs the design on its own, then orchestrates the build along three paths: itself, delegate tasks on models it chooses, or the swarm. A Writer on Sonnet writes specs, plans and tasks in Spec Kit's layout, and a Judge on Opus reviews them. A parallel swarm of Haiku, Sonnet and Opus implementers builds them, each attempt supervised and every merge made one at a time. With superdelegation on, everything that is not the Lead runs first on the quota of other harnesses, such as agy or grok, and native Claude is the fallback. With the owner's permission, the Lead works for hours and ends with a brief.

superdelegation.title: Superdelegation
superdelegation.description: Send everything that is not the Lead to other harnesses (agy, grok, muse, ...) while their quota lasts; native Claude is the fallback. It covers the swarm, the design seats and the Lead's delegate tasks: the ones that only read go to the harness the one rule picks, and the ones that edit files go first to another harness on a worktree of their own, which the Lead merges. Off by default: the external CLIs run without permission prompts and spend other plans' quota. Linux only. Replaces the lanes and seats options.

lanes.title: Lanes (legacy)
lanes.description: Replaced by superdelegation. Read only when superdelegation is not set: on counts as superdelegation on.

harnesses.title: Lane harnesses
harnesses.description: The external harnesses superdelegation may use, comma-separated: agy, codex, grok, cursor, muse. The quota decides the order of the candidates, then the cost per task. Default: agy. Each one runs its CLI without permission prompts in Aether's transactional worktree, with your git, GitHub, package-registry and cloud credentials kept out of its environment. Turn one on only once you accept that risk.

ops.title: Ops in the mod
ops.description: Run the swarm's own aether-wt and aether-lane commands in the mod, without a model. On by default. Turn it off when your project's test command needs your shell's environment, which the mod's does not have: the Haiku ops agent then runs them with the Bash tool, as before 0.8.

seats.title: Design seats (legacy)
seats.description: Ignored. The design seats follow superdelegation now; native, balanced and robust no longer exist.

deadlines.title: Delegate time limits
deadlines.description: How long a delegate task waits, in seconds, for the quota decision, written as quota=3; a value above 10 counts as 10. Default: quota=3.

quotabrake.title: Quota brake
quotabrake.description: The percent of the five-hour window used at which the quota brake acts in a Lead session: it warns you and, in an autonomous run, pauses the run until the window resets, then resumes it. The seven-day window at the same percent only warns. Only your own words turn the brake off for a run. Default: 95.

brakepush.title: Push saved unit branches
brakepush.description: Also push the unit branches an interrupted workflow saved to origin. Off by default: saved work stays on its local branch. A push still needs your recorded push permission each time.

observedev.title: Self-observation development mode
observedev.description: Turn on development mode for self-observation, which also keeps redacted conversation fragments around failures and owner corrections to the Lead. Off by default: standard self-observation never reads or keeps conversation text.
